title: Therapeutic ultrasound
what: A specialist moves a probe over your skin that sends ultrasound deep into the tissues. Sometimes a medicated gel is used.
why: For pain in joints, ligaments, and muscles, after injuries, and for scars, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: a session usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; a course is usually about 10 sessions
tell_doctor: If you have a pacemaker or metal implants in that area
Wounds or a rash on the skin

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Skin should be clean, with no cream.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that lets you uncover the area.

bring: Tissues to wipe off the gel
steps: Gel is put on the skin
The specialist slowly moves the probe over the sore area
Sometimes it is done in water, for fingers and feet
At the end, the gel is wiped off
feel: Usually nothing but the touch of the probe
Sometimes mild warmth. If it feels hot or hurts, say so right away
after: You can return to normal activities right away
Come to sessions on schedule. The full course matters
red_flags: Pain or burning in the treated area that does not go away: tell your doctor

faq.q: Is this the same as an ultrasound scan?
faq.a: No. A scan uses ultrasound to look inside. This uses it to treat. The devices and power are different.

faq.q: Can it be done with metal in the bone?
faq.a: Usually it is limited in that area. Tell your doctor, and they will decide.

reminders.text: Ultrasound therapy today. No cream on your skin. Bring your referral.
